sections.title: Toolbars
sections.notes: Introductory description only.

checks.statement: Use toolbars to display frequently used actions relevant to the current page; they may contain varied controls and can pair with a FAB to emphasize an action. Do not show a toolbar and navigation bar at the same time.
checks.condition: When choosing or configuring a toolbar.

sourceHistory.summary: Overview states toolbar purpose, control flexibility, FAB pairing, and navigation-bar exclusion.

checks.statement: Replace the still-supported but no-longer-recommended bottom app bar with the shorter, more flexible docked toolbar. Use a floating toolbar for more actions and flexible placement; it may be horizontal or vertical, use standard or vibrant color, contain many controls, and pair with a FAB. Use vibrant styling for emphasis.
checks.condition: When selecting M3 Expressive toolbar variants.

sourceHistory.summary: Expressive update describes variant recommendation, flexibility, color styles, orientation, and FAB pairing.

checks.statement: M3 bottom app bars use updated dynamic color mappings, have a taller container, no shadow, and contain the FAB within the bar rather than leaving it outside.
checks.condition: When implementing baseline M3 bottom app-bar behavior or comparing with M2.

sourceHistory.summary: M2 comparison enumerates color, elevation, height, and FAB containment changes.

checks.statement: M3 Expressive provides docked and floating toolbars. The baseline bottom app bar is available in M3 but remains supported and is not recommended in Expressive; use the docked toolbar instead. On Jetpack Compose, the floating toolbar is a separate component from the docked toolbar and bottom app bar.
checks.condition: When selecting toolbar variants by version and platform.

sourceHistory.summary: Variant table and note distinguish availability, recommendation, and Compose component boundaries.

checks.statement: M3 Expressive supports standard (default) and vibrant colors, horizontal (default) and vertical floating layouts, and a floating toolbar with FAB. M3 provides standard color and FAB only as a bottom app bar. Jetpack Compose fully supports floating toolbar with FAB; on other platforms, add the toolbar and FAB separately.
checks.condition: When selecting toolbar color/layout and FAB configurations for a platform.

sourceHistory.summary: Configuration table preserves version availability and the platform-specific FAB implementation boundary.

checks.statement: Treat a toolbar as a container with configurable slots; slots may contain different elements, commonly icon buttons, buttons, and text fields.
checks.condition: When arranging toolbar controls.

sourceHistory.summary: Slots guidance describes the container model and common slot contents.

checks.statement: By default, toolbars are 64dp high, center-aligned, use equal padding between items, and have at least 16dp outside padding. Docked-toolbar alignment and padding may be configured for the layout.
checks.condition: When sizing or aligning a docked toolbar.

sourceHistory.summary: Measurements introduction gives toolbar defaults and docked diagrams show configurable alignment/padding; exact image-only values remain unavailable.

checks.statement: Use a toolbar for actions related to the current page. Use a docked toolbar across the window for global actions that persist across pages and a floating toolbar above body content for contextual page actions. When actions do not fit, add a menu. Standard colors keep emphasis on content; vibrant colors emphasize controls or can signal a temporary mode such as editing. Consider alternative color roles for app-specific emphasis.
checks.condition: When choosing toolbar variant and color emphasis.

sourceHistory.summary: Usage maps docked/floating variants to global/contextual actions and defines color emphasis and overflow.

checks.statement: Do not show toolbar and navigation bar together. Show navigation bars on primary pages and toolbars with actions on subsequent pages; floating toolbars may provide local navigation between related subsequent pages, but avoid redundant or confusing navigation combinations.
checks.condition: When a product uses both bottom navigation and toolbar navigation.

sourceHistory.summary: Guidance separates navigation bar and toolbar by page hierarchy and cautions against duplicate navigation.

checks.statement: A docked toolbar spans the window width and uses straight corners. Keep at least 16dp padding on each outer edge; 32dp between items is the default but may change. Give each element at least a 48×48dp target and avoid overwhelming people with too many controls. Keep a floating toolbar fully onscreen; move excess actions to an overflow menu.
checks.condition: When sizing or arranging docked or floating toolbar controls.

sourceHistory.summary: Container guidance covers shape, width, padding, target size, control count, and floating overflow.

checks.statement: Floating toolbars have elevation by default; it may be removed when the background beneath them is visually distinct.
checks.condition: When a floating toolbar sits on a visually distinct background.

sourceHistory.summary: Elevation guidance defines default and conditional removal.

checks.statement: Slots may contain buttons, icon buttons, images, text fields, or custom components. Use icon buttons for an even hierarchy; emphasize no more than one action, using button style/color, size, or a FAB. Avoid mixing many control designs and avoid square icon buttons in floating toolbars; square buttons are allowed in docked toolbars.
checks.condition: When composing and emphasizing toolbar actions.

sourceHistory.summary: Slots guidance lists element types and rules for hierarchy, emphasis, consistency, and square buttons.

checks.statement: A FAB may sit next to a floating toolbar to present one high-priority action alongside a unified set of toolbar actions.
checks.condition: When one primary action should accompany a floating toolbar.

sourceHistory.summary: FAB guidance describes pairing and action hierarchy.

checks.statement: Place docked toolbars only at the bottom and do not use them alongside another bottom-aligned element such as a navigation bar. Floating toolbars may be horizontal or vertical; keep horizontal ones at least 16dp from the window edge and vertical ones at least 24dp away. At larger breakpoints, vertical toolbars may sit on either side opposite a navigation rail; use narrow/default icon buttons and center the rail when both appear. Avoid vertical floating toolbars in compact layouts unless the screen is simple or has few controls.
checks.condition: When positioning toolbar variants across layouts.

sourceHistory.summary: Position guidance specifies bottom placement, orientations, edge margins, navigation-rail relation, button width, and compact caution.

checks.statement: A docked toolbar spans 100% of the screen. Space items evenly in compact windows. At medium and larger breakpoints, center items or center a key action while moving other items to the edges. On web and large screens it may be rounded and subdivided with dividers; reduce height and use XS controls only when vertical space is limited.
checks.condition: When adapting docked toolbars across breakpoints.

sourceHistory.summary: Docked resizing guidance covers width, compact spacing, large-screen arrangements, and conditional dense layout.

checks.statement: Size a floating toolbar only as large as its contents while preserving a 16dp margin; cap its width if needed. Put overflow actions in a trailing-slot menu and reveal more actions at larger breakpoints. Avoid vertical floating toolbars in compact windows except for simple screens or few controls.
checks.condition: When adapting floating toolbars to available space.

sourceHistory.summary: Floating resizing guidance covers content-sized width, margin, overflow, reveal behavior, and compact caution.

checks.statement: At larger breakpoints, multiple floating toolbars may be placed on opposite edges to group distinct actions, with styling used to clarify hierarchy. Do not use multiple toolbars in compact windows; use one toolbar. Trailing actions may collapse to overflow at smaller breakpoints and reappear at larger sizes.
checks.condition: When presenting multiple toolbars or adapting action count.

sourceHistory.summary: Presentation guidance distinguishes large-screen grouping from compact limits and adaptive overflow.

checks.statement: In RTL, mirror individual elements such as icons and text direction; when action order matters, reverse the action order so trailing actions stay at the trailing edge.
checks.condition: When localizing toolbar layouts to RTL.

sourceHistory.summary: RTL guidance specifies element mirroring and conditional action-order reversal.

checks.statement: Docked toolbars may remain fixed or animate offscreen. Floating toolbars may remain, animate offscreen, or collapse into one high-emphasis action on scroll; Jetpack Compose supports collapsing to a FAB or key action. Do not collapse actions while also transitioning the toolbar offscreen.
checks.condition: When toolbar behavior responds to page scrolling.

sourceHistory.summary: Scrolling guidance lists variant options, Compose capability, and incompatible simultaneous transitions.

checks.statement: Assistive-technology users must be able to navigate to and activate toolbar actions, select menu destinations, activate a back button, and retain access to controls while content scrolls or collapses.
checks.condition: For accessible toolbars.

sourceHistory.summary: Use cases list action, destination, back, and persistence tasks.

checks.statement: Toolbars have no interactions by default; placed controls provide interaction. Tapping icon buttons gives ripple feedback; hover shows an interactive cue and clicking gives ripple feedback.
checks.condition: When controls inside a toolbar are touched or used with a cursor.

sourceHistory.summary: Interaction guidance assigns behavior to child elements and describes touch/cursor feedback.

checks.statement: Place initial focus on the first interactive element and allow Tab to move through the remaining actions.
checks.condition: When a toolbar receives keyboard focus.

sourceHistory.summary: Initial-focus guidance specifies first control and subsequent Tab navigation.

checks.statement: Tab or arrow keys move between interactive elements; Space or Enter activates the focused element.
checks.condition: When keyboard-operating a toolbar.

sourceHistory.summary: Keyboard table maps navigation and activation keys.

checks.statement: Expose the toolbar container with the toolbar role on web; on mobile it may be a generic container. Give each action the accessibility treatment required by its own component guidance.
checks.condition: When exposing a toolbar and its controls to assistive technology.

sourceHistory.summary: Labeling guidance defines the web role, mobile option, and child-control delegation.
